searchText: <@427491045308235776> Plop. Just saw that gokzg changed the definition of a Blob to be a dynamic type. Any particular reason for this? With no major version change, anyone who depends on go-ethereum as a library now gets a broken dep hierarchy, because Go just fetches the new gokzg Which is not backwards compatible with the old one Hey, prysm wanted a way to do both Mainnet tests and Minimal tests Are the minimal tests different blob sizes? yeah kind of annoying that go doesn’t respect semver, pre 1.0 Yeah they are not 4096, they are sized 4 Was just wondering if this is long term teh direction and then just pull the change ourselves too Ok, will open a PR to update our code too thx Will you be okay with supporting minimal configs too? Alright let me know when the PR is open and I can review No, I just need to unfuckup the types 😄 I just need to fix https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/issues/28285 Curious question tho, do we need to support minimal configs? I guess yes But how does that work? That would mean blobs thoughout can be arbitrary size Does CKZG support it? We depend on both libs, so that's would be a prerequisite Oh, btw > Because we use generics, the minimum golang version is 1.18, which seems to be fairly conservative. However, if a lower version is needed, replacing the generics is fairly straightforward. Go only backports security fixes to one previous version (e.g. now 1.21 and 1.20), so my suggestion is - especially for crypto libs - to be very agressive in cutting off old versions of Go. You won't be able to track what weird big.Int bug isn't hotfixed and how it might impact you. It’s mainly used for testing, so technically no, but it’s a CL concept that I think most EL clients are looking to support CKzg currently supports it but required a separate compile to get it working, I’ll check if that’s changed to compile time Good point — I didn’t want to be too aggressive and maybe cause issues for geth which may be more conservative with the minimum supported geth version We only ever support the last 2 versions of Go due to the same reasons +it allows us to semi-reasonably fast use new features of the language I mean, it's up to you. Just saying what we do and why 🙂 <@206016661470314496> If geth doesn’t plan to support minimal, let me go back to the previous minor bump and then open a conversation with prysm as to how we can move forward You won’t need to make any changes in that respects Do you have a rundown of what exactly minimal would need from EL side? I'm somewhat reluctant though to support it if there's no real network need behind it Mainly to support two blob sizes, which implies two trusted setup files and two initialiser methods I’m not aware of anything else, though <@755590043632140352> can give more context here The second trusted setup for minimal is small because you only need to support blobs of size 4. You can probably hide that complexity by using the init in go-kzg that embeds the minimal trusted setup Have made two releases: - 0.5.0 fixes the issue by going back to mainnet only blobs - 0.6.0 bumps the MSGV and updates the policy to what you noted above. We now test for 1.18, one version behind latest and latest. I cherrypicked the changes for minimal onto a new branch (opened a PR) so that prysm folks are not completely blocked while we discuss support for minimal. Does geth support trusted setup files via flags already? e.g in Teku: ` - --Xtrusted-setup=/network-config/trusted_setup.txt`. We use that to change setup files early on when things weren't stable yet. But if the feature exists, then you don't need to do anything to support minimal tests since the test runner can pass a minimal trusted setup file. It doesn't look like you can change it currently as it uses go:embed -- so main thing to implement would be a runtime flag and the change to slices Afaik there's no real network need for it. However a big chunk of our testing depends on minimal configs. Prysm runs a network from genesis and runs all forks on CI, for this we use minimal configs or it would take several hours per run. Other test environments like antithesis also run on minimal configs. It's not really required that geth supports it but it would make our life much easier instead of having to fork presumably geth just for our testing environment Probably posted in the wrong channel, so reposting here, I think we can safely make minimal and mainnet blob sizes be the same, this should require no changes to client codes and no addition of runtime checks. CC <@415109946682769408> do you feel anything against this on the pyspec tests?

excerpts.author: karalabe
excerpts.content:
Oh, btw

> Because we use generics, the minimum golang version is 1.18, which seems to be fairly conservative. However, if a lower version is needed, replacing the generics is fairly straightforward.

Go only backports security fixes to one previous version (e.g. now 1.21 and 1.20), so my suggestion is - especially for crypto libs - to be very agressive in cutting off old versions of Go. You won't be able to track what weird big.Int bug isn't hotfixed and how it might impact you.

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
It’s mainly used for testing, so technically no, but it’s a CL concept that I think most EL clients are looking to support

CKzg currently supports it but required a separate compile to get it working, I’ll check if that’s changed to compile time

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: Good point — I didn’t want to be too aggressive and maybe cause issues for geth which may be more conservative with the minimum supported geth version

I’m not aware of anything else, though <@755590043632140352> can give more context here

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: The second trusted setup for minimal is small because you only need to support blobs of size 4. You can probably hide that complexity by using the init in go-kzg that embeds the minimal trusted setup

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
Have made two releases:

- 0.5.0 fixes the issue by going back to mainnet only blobs
- 0.6.0 bumps the MSGV and updates the policy to what you noted above. We now test for 1.18, one version behind latest and latest.

I cherrypicked the changes for minimal onto a new branch (opened a PR) so that prysm folks are not completely blocked while we discuss support for minimal.

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
Does geth support trusted setup files via flags already?
e.g in Teku: `  - --Xtrusted-setup=/network-config/trusted_setup.txt`. We use that to change setup files early on when things weren't stable yet. But if the feature exists, then you don't need to do anything to support minimal tests since the test runner can pass a minimal trusted setup file.

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content: It doesn't look like you can change it currently as it uses go:embed -- so main thing to implement would be a runtime flag and the change to slices

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Afaik there's no real network need for it. However a big chunk of our testing depends on minimal configs. Prysm runs a network from genesis and runs all forks on CI, for this we use minimal configs or it would take several hours per run. Other test environments like antithesis also run on minimal configs. It's not really required that geth supports it but it would make our life much easier instead of having to fork presumably geth just for our testing environment
